recent_articles.title: Kerala High Court wins e-governance award - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Kerala High Court** has been awarded the Gold Award for its District Court Case Management System (DCMS) at the National e-Governance Awards, 2026. The award recognizes DCMS's innovative use of AI and other new age technologies to provide citizen-centric services.  This comprehensive platform, developed by the **Kerala High Court**'s IT Directorate, manages case lifecycles from filing to disposal and beyond.  The system has been implemented across district judiciary in Kerala and the Union Territory of Lakshadweep, with a goal of transitioning all courts to paperless functioning.

recent_articles.title: In Kashmir, a stir over Mehbooba’s ‘review’ of AIIMS | India News - The Indian Express

The party's spokesperson, Tanvir Sadiq, stated that the PDP is being reactivated to counter the NC's demands for statehood restoration. **People’s Conference** president Sajad Lone criticized Mufti's visit as a constitutional crisis, while MLA Waheed ur Rehman Para questioned the project's delay and criticized the chief minister for prioritizing party affairs over healthcare. The over Rs 2,000 crore project was announced in 2015 under the Prime Minister’s Development Package (PMDP).

recent_articles.title: National Awards for e-Governance 2026 | UPSC Knowledge Nugget
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union government** has announced the winners of the 29th National Conference on e-Governance, recognizing excellence in e-governance initiatives. The awards include a trophy, certificate, and an incentive for Gold awardees.  This year's winners are projects from various ministries including the Agriculture Ministry's AgriStack platform, the Consumer Affairs Ministry's e-Jagriti portal, and the Prayagraj Mela Authority's conduct of the Mahakumbh 2025. E-governance in India has evolved since computerization in the 1970s, with key milestones including the establishment of the National Informatics Centre (NIC) and the launch of the National e-Governance Plan (NeGP).  Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), a set of foundational digital systems, plays a crucial role in modern society. India's DPI is built on the JAM trinity—Jan Dhan bank accounts, Aadhaar enrolment, and widespread mobile phone penetration.

recent_articles.title: Ladakh eases excise rules, expands hard liquor sales to boost tourism | India News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lieutenant Governor V K Saxena** approved a new excise policy for **Ladakh**, which allows the retail sale of hard liquor and expands liquor outlets from two to twenty. The policy aims to reduce dependence on narcotics, strengthen regulation, and support tourism-led economic activity.  The policy also seeks to optimize excise revenue in a transparent manner, addressing concerns about limited availability of brands and outlets that led to tourists resorting to illegal substances.

recent_articles.title: No inquiry needed: J-K High Court says President, Governor can terminate govt employees over ‘security of state’ | India News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.sentiment_target: Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh High Court
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh High Court** has upheld the dismissal of a police constable, Ghulam Mohammad Tantray, by the then Governor based on Article 311(2)(c) of the Constitution. The court ruled that the President or Governor can remove employees from government service without an inquiry if it is deemed necessary for the security of the state.  The court acknowledged that this provision has a high threshold and requires subjective satisfaction, considering factors like terrorism, espionage, or anti-national conduct. This decision comes amidst criticism of the Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor's administration for dismissing 91 employees under Article 311(2)(c) since 2021.

recent_articles.title: Pahalgam: Let the valley remain pristine
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Jammu and Kashmir**'s Pahalgam, a popular tourist resort, is facing environmental problems due to unscientific garbage disposal. The landfill site at Sarbal contaminates the Nallah Tulyan stream, which flows into the Lidder river, posing risks to aquatic life and water quality.  Environmental activists like **Mushtaq Pahalgami** have been advocating for its closure for years, citing concerns about forest land usage and ecological damage. Despite government assurances, no significant action has been taken to relocate the landfill. The issue highlights the need for sustainable waste management practices in tourist destinations to protect fragile ecosystems.

recent_articles.title: SIR enumeration phase begins in Odisha, Mizoram, Sikkim and Manipur, says EC | Today News

The **Election Commission** emphasizes that the SIR exercise aims to ensure accurate and comprehensive voter lists, including all eligible citizens aged 18 and above while removing ineligible individuals.

recent_articles.title: Over 300 tourists stranded in Gulmarg’s high-altitude cable cars rescued - The Hindu

The cable car is expected to remain closed for maintenance on May 26th and 27th, with ticket refunds issued for those dates.
